method: Live browser on databento.com/pricing and databento.com/datasets/GLBX.MDP3. JS pricing page + dataset Availability details. Docs/blog for 2010 backfill and StatType.

pricing.model: usage-based historical $/GB uncompressed binary; subscription optional
pricing.credits_expire: 6 months after signup; one set per team
pricing.credits_apply_to: historical data from any dataset; also first month of a plan if used that way
pricing.standard_note: CME Standard. Live included. Do not open for V6 first pass.
pricing.usage_usd_per_gb: NOT_A_SINGLE_PUBLIC_NUMBER. Use metadata.get_cost after API key.
pricing.metering: outbound uncompressed binary GB. Metadata/symbology/account are free. Definition cost accurate on 24h multiples.
pricing.live_usage_based: deprecated for most datasets; live needs license. V6 is historical only.

license.historical: Click-wrap Databento + exchange terms at signup. Internal research typical. No raw redistribution.
license.live: self-service questionnaire + pass-through exchange license. Not needed for V6.
license.commercial_use_on_usage_based_historical: personal and commercial listed on pricing comparison; redistribution is Plus+

api.auth: HTTP Basic, API key as username, empty password
api.python_client: databento.Historical; optional. TradeMind uses stdlib HTTP.

dataset.name: CME Globex MDP 3.0
dataset.origin: Aurora DC3 FPGA capture after 2017-05-21; FIX flat files / CME DataMine before that. No capture timestamps pre-2017-05-21. Millisecond timestamps before 2015-11-20.

release.historical: delayed 20 minutes or 8 hours depending on access listed on dataset page

schemas.note: UTC date electronic session OHLC. Not official settlement.
settlement=3 cleared_volume=6 open_interest=9. OI usually next UTC date.
Not in first purchase. Highest granularity only after MDP 3.0.

symbol_first_last.note: Per-root first/last requires metadata.get_dataset_range or a parent pull after API key. Venue dataset start is 2010-06-06 for ohlcv-1d/definition/statistics.

do_not: use continuous-only series as the PRODUCTION curve
